subject: Throttle warning & mitigation slate — ClearBridge reserved throughput drop
body:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@clearbridge.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Throttle warning & mitigation slate — ClearBridge reserved throughput drop

Alex —

Quick heads-up from last night: our dedicated GPU pool serving ClearBridge started showing sustained token-queue growth around 02:40 PDT, and by 03:20 we observed a 25% hit to effective reserved throughput for their model route. That translated to latency tail increases for several critical endpoints in their flow.

Id like to propose a short mitigation slate and get exec visibility if we need to request emergency burst credits:

- Immediate: enable fallback to v2-quant (compatible variant) for sampling-heavy routes (estimated 15-20% throughput recovery)
- 30 min: ramp a temporary canary of additional dedicated workers (manual burst) to buy headroom
- 2 hrs: ops will stitch KV-cache prefixes for the top 20 request prefixes to reduce repeated compute
- Sales/Finance ask: prepare an emergency burst-credit approval (if canary insufficient)

Ive attached the QPS timeline and a short CSV with queue depth samples. Can we sync at 10:00 PT?

Thanks,
Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0193

---

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@clearbridge.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: SRE Team <sre@clearbridge.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2027 09:37:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Throttle warning & mitigation slate — ClearBridge reserved throughput drop

Thanks Hannah — appreciate the flag.

A couple notes from our side:
- We observed spike in batched inference calls tied to a nightly report job; that job sends longer contexts and has been running at a higher parallelism than expected since last config change on 9/20.
- We can throttle the report job on our end immediately (will do now) but were concerned about hitting the contract reservation floor during peak business hours.

10:00 PT works for quick sync. If you think burst credits will be needed, please outline the dollar estimate so I can escalate internally.

Alex
Alex Rivera
Head of Platform Engineering, ClearBridge Financial
alex.rivera@clearbridge.com

---

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@clearbridge.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2027 10:03:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Throttle warning & mitigation slate — ClearBridge reserved throughput drop

Looping in a few quick operational details before our sync:

- Root cause (ops triage): burst of long-context batched jobs + an emergent kernel-path on the GPU runtime that prevents effective continuous batching for >2k token requests. The runtime falls back to a slower path for these requests, which explains the sudden per-token cost and queueing.
- Immediate mitigation we've queued: enable prefix-level KV caching for the nightly-report route (expect ~12% latency tail improvement) and activate the v2-quant fallback for the next 90 minutes.
- If the canary shows less than 10% headroom recovery, we recommend approving a 48-hour manual burst (estimated cost: $8k) to prevent SLA violation while engineering patches the kernel selector.

During the sync well present the telemetry snapshot and a quick runbook for re-routing critical endpoints.

-L

Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

---

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@clearbridge.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2027 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throttle warning & mitigation slate — ClearBridge reserved throughput drop

Follow-up from engineering after the 10:00 sync:

- Canary v2-quant rollback recovered ~18% of throughput within 25 minutes; prefix caching added another ~9% improvement to mean latency and reduced 5xx incidence from 1.8% to 0.3% on the sampled routes.
- The kernel selector patch is low-risk but needs a staged deploy; ops recommends a staggered roll starting 01:00 UTC tomorrow to avoid impacting other high-throughput tenants.
- Given expected traffic tomorrow morning (billing window), we recommend approving the 48-hour manual burst authorization to keep headroom above contract floor. Finance estimate attached; were requesting an urgent approval path via CS leadership.

Action items:
1) Alex: confirm ClearBridge can temporarily throttle the nightly-report or move its execution window (ack received from Alex at 17:50).
2) Hannah & Lauren: pursue exec authorization for $8k 48-hour burst (Hannah to draft the justification).
3) Engineering: begin staged deploy of kernel selector patch at 01:00 UTC tomorrow.

Ill keep the thread updated with telemetry after the deploy.

-David

David Kim
VP, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
david_kim@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: clearbridge_qps_report.csv (QPS samples 02:00-06:00 PDT), timeline_screenshot.png (queue depth visualization)
